analysis:
Reviewed the two head_text excerpts of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (lines 317-907). The PR's patch changes are documentation only: the 'Last updated' date, and `load_model` / `prefetch_model` text stating that a model outside the operator filter is refused with `model_not_selected` (`autopilotAllowsModel`). Those changed ranges (head 1412-1424, 1456-1464) fall outside the supplied excerpts, and the patch excerpt is truncated, so the full new text is unverified. The excerpts I did see are unchanged context. They cover register cluster_membership and busy fields, heartbeat, backend_capacity telemetry, service reservation release, inference_error sanitization, and attestation_response.

No code, key handling, encryption, attestation or authorization logic changes in the reviewed units. The one security-relevant direction is the operator filter as a provider-side restriction on coordinator-initiated load/prefetch. It narrows the surface (TB-002, A-004, T-012) and adds no weakening. It does not affect A-016 or T-053 authorization.

Open integration questions: (1) the operator-filter semantics and the `model_not_selected` refusal live in provider code and configuration.md, not in the supplied evidence. I cannot confirm the docs match enforcement, though a doc-only mismatch is not a security regression. (2) Whether filter refusal happens before any download or load, as the new prefetch text claims; confirm it in the provider handler. The excerpts show no threat-model gap requiring an update.
